title: Calendar Whiplash
blurb: History's timeline, but somebody shuffled it. Three are real. One is cap.

cards.say: Betty White [was born before sliced bread was first sold], [was born closer to the Civil War than to the first iPhone], [hosted the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade for 20 years], and [had a TV career that Guinness measured at 79 years].
cards.real: She co-hosted NBC's Macy's parade coverage for about ten years, 1962 to 1971. Her 20-year run was as a commentator for the Rose Parade.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sliced_bread (first sold July 7, 1928; she was born January 17, 1922, per the Mental Floss page)

https://www.mentalfloss.com/article/61054/15-things-you-didnt-know-about-betty-white (born January 17, 1922; arithmetic: 57 years after the Civil War ended in 1865, 85 years before the first iPhone in 2007)

cards.say: The lighter [had its most famous version, the Zippo, invented during World War II], [was invented before the friction match], [had an early model that made its own hydrogen gas from zinc and acid], and [was invented while Beethoven was still alive].
cards.real: George Blaisdell invented the Zippo in 1932 in Bradford, Pennsylvania, seven years before World War II began.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: Beethoven died in March 1827; the lamp's 1823 date is confirmed here) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C3%B6bereiner%27s_lamp

cards.say: Queen Victoria [was born while Napoleon was still alive], [proposed to Prince Albert, not the other way around], [lived long enough to be filmed with a movie camera], and [was still on the throne when the Wright brothers first flew].
cards.real: Victoria died in January 1901, almost three years before the Wright brothers' first flight in December 1903.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon (died May 5, 1821; Victoria born May 24, 1819 per https://www.royalmint.com/discover/uk-coins/victoria-200/queen-victoria---a-remarkable-life-and-reign/)
https://replay.bfi.org.uk/video/c54272df-aada-529c-b4e6-d583938883fe (Scenes at Balmoral, filmed by Downey in 1896)

cards.say: Santa Fe [was founded before the Pilgrims reached Plymouth], [became the capital of the 48th state in 1912], [was briefly held by Confederate troops in 1862], and [was founded while Shakespeare was still alive].
cards.real: New Mexico became the 47th state in January 1912, with Santa Fe as its capital. Arizona was the 48th, a month later.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe,_New_Mexico (new city founded 1607, made capital 1610; the Pilgrims landed in 1620)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe,_New_Mexico (Confederate forces held the city in March 1862)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1616 (Shakespeare died April 23, 1616; Santa Fe founded 1607 to 1610)

cards.say: The fax machine [was patented before the telephone], [was patented before the first photograph was taken], [was first patented by a Scottish clockmaker], and [had a public line running in France during the US Civil War].
cards.real: The oldest surviving camera photograph was made in 1827. Alexander Bain's fax patent came 16 years later, in 1843.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Bain_(inventor) (patent of May 27, 1843; Bell's telephone patent was 1876)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pantelegraph (Paris-Lyon line open to the public from February 1863)

cards.say: Iolani Palace [had electric lights before the White House did], [was finished before the Eiffel Tower], [served as Hawaii's government headquarters until 1969], and [had a telephone before the White House did].
cards.real: The White House got its first telephone in 1877. Iolani Palace wasn't even finished until 1882.
src: https://ethw.org/Milestones:Electric_Lighting_Of_The_Kingdom_of_Hawaii_1886-1888 (1887, four years before the White House)

cards.say: The Brooklyn Bridge [opened after the Statue of Liberty was unveiled], [opened before the Washington Monument was finished], [was crossed by 21 of P.T. Barnum's elephants in 1884], and [wasn't officially named the Brooklyn Bridge until 1915].
cards.real: The bridge opened in May 1883. The Statue of Liberty wasn't dedicated until October 1886, three and a half years later.
src: https://www.newworldencyclopedia.org/entry/Statue_of_Liberty (dedicated October 28, 1886; bridge opened May 24, 1883 per the NYPL page)

cards.say: Ida May Fuller [was born while Ulysses S. Grant was president], [went to school with future president Calvin Coolidge], [got the first monthly Social Security check in 1935], and [was still collecting Social Security after the 1969 Moon landing].
cards.real: Her check, number 00-000-001, was dated January 31, 1940. The Social Security Act passed in 1935, but monthly checks began in 1940.

cards.say: Alice Liddell [was born before Abraham Lincoln became president], [spent her 80th birthday as guest of honor at Columbia University], [was still alive when Mickey Mouse made his debut], and [was 15 when Lewis Carroll first told her the Wonderland story].
cards.real: She was 10 on the July 1862 boat trip when Carroll first told her the story that became Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

cards.say: Levi's jeans [were first made for miners in the 1849 Gold Rush], [were patented before Edison's light bulb], [were called waist overalls, not jeans, until about 1960], and [were the idea of a tailor who bought cloth from Levi Strauss].
cards.real: Levi Strauss didn't reach San Francisco until 1853, and the riveted pants we call jeans were patented in 1873.

cards.say: Newgrange [is older than the Great Pyramid of Giza], [is older than Stonehenge], [was lined up to catch the sunrise on the summer solstice], and [picks who gets to watch its solstice sunrise from inside by lottery].
cards.real: Newgrange catches the sunrise around the winter solstice in December, when a beam lights its inner chamber for about 17 minutes.

cards.say: Concorde [made its first flight before anyone walked on the Moon], [cruised at three times the speed of sound], [once chased a solar eclipse so astronomers could watch it for 74 minutes], and [carried its last passengers before the first YouTube video was posted].
cards.real: Concorde cruised at twice the speed of sound, about 1,350 miles per hour, and crossed the Atlantic in around three and a half hours.
